summary: iOS renders a load-error state with a gray warning triangle, "Could not load member," supporting text, and a compact outlined Retry button instead of the React profile content.

The React header shows a purple square avatar, bold "artin," monospaced "@artin," and a trailing conversation/person icon; iOS instead uses a larger bold "Member" title and gray monospaced "Profile" subtitle with no avatar or trailing action.
The iOS body omits the large avatar/name block, Description/Owner section, Info and Role controls, email, joined date, Created Agents section, and the coral Remove Member button.
React content is dense and top-aligned with inset section dividers and a near-content-width danger button; iOS leaves most of the body blank and centers a much smaller error group.
iOS uses only black and gray for the visible content, while React uses purple for both avatars, gray metadata and labels, and coral-red for the destructive action.
likelyCauses: The iOS member request is failing, returning no data, or mapping an invalid response to the error state.
The React and iOS captures are using different test fixtures, credentials, or API states.
The iOS route may be passing a missing or mismatched member identifier to the member-detail request.
suggestedFixes: Provide the iOS capture with the same successful member payload as React and verify the route member ID, endpoint, and response parsing.
Ensure the successful state renders the complete profile body, including avatar, identity, description, role, email, joined date, agents, and Remove Member action.
Match the React header structure and alignment: compact avatar/name content and trailing action, or update both platforms to one approved header design.
Match the approved typography, avatar shape and color, section spacing, divider bounds, and action-button width/radius/color across platforms.
Keep the load-error UI only for genuine failures and cover it with a separate deterministic error-state test.

Match header-button size, fill, stroke, corner radius, icon style, and spacing to the shared 390-point design.
Use consistent popup anchoring, width, row height, padding, shadow, and border tokens; account for the extra React menu row.
Align the Profile tab, profile header, status indicator, chips, and conditional capture banner across platforms.
Normalize typography and metadata layout, then crop/scale the iOS capture to the same component-bounds viewport before testing.
